item.title: Chapman thanks trainer and donors after 'freak' injury
item.description: Boxer Raven Chapman believes the fast actions of trainer Stuart Scott may have saved her life when she suffered a bleed on the brain over the summer. The 32-year-old was airlifted to hospital and placed in a medically induced coma following a sparring session in Denmark on 24 July. Chapman had collapsed after training and was taken to hospital after Scott called for an ambulance, to be later diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema. "I remember the final spar where it happened, It was the third spar of the week and I felt fine going in there," she told BBC South Today. "It was just a sort of freak injury that I never thought it would happen to me, we (herself and Scott) have done hundreds of sparring rounds together and my fights. "He knows the kind of things that I say and I wasn't acting myself from what he said, that's when he called an ambulance before anything even happened. "I sat down and then it all sort of happened after that, luckily with where I was at the time, I think in under an hour from when the ambulance was called I was then into surgery." After reaching hospital, the procedure Chapman underwent successfully stemmed the bleeding in her brain and helped to stabilise the swelling. A fundraiser was then launched online for people to contribute towards getting her back to the UK and her long-term recovery. A total of £97,792 was donated after the page was shared widely among the boxing community on social media. Chapman's promoters Queensberry, Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn and Most Valuable Promotions' Nakisa Bidarian were among the leading donors. "All the support that I got was just amazing," Chapman added. "That's why, with all the fundraising money, I'm going to use that to make sure I'm getting everything so that I get better as that's why people donated. "It brings a tear to your eye when you see it and how much people are there for you in the community, it's a special world, the boxing world." Chapman 'gutted' at not being able to achieve dreams Raven Chapman was promoted by Frank Warren's Queensberry Promotions [Getty Images] Norwich-born Chapman trains at Warriors Gym in High Wycombe and as a professional won 10 of her 12 fights with just two defeats. At one stage of her career she was based in Bournemouth, training alongside former WBO cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith, who was one of many professional boxers to share a video message of support for her. Chapman lost to Skye Nicolson in a bid to win the WBC featherweight belt in October 2024 , the only women's world title fight ever to be held in Saudi Arabia. She admitted that not being able to now achieve what she had hoped in the sport will to be difficult to come to terms with. "I probably would never get a licence again after this," Chapman said. "Even if they said I could, I probably wouldn't want to risk putting my loved ones through that pain of it again. item.title: Ducks star Leo Carlsson hits major scoring milestone during Canucks game
item.description: Marc DesRosiers-IMAGN Images Ducks star Leo Carlsson hits major scoring milestone during Canucks game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Anaheim Ducks forward Leo Carlsson reached a career milestone during Tuesday’s 6-5 overtime loss to the Vancouver Canucks at Honda Center. The 21-year-old scored his 65th NHL goal, moving past Lucas Raymond for the second-most goals by a Swedish player before turning 22. Mats Sundin remains the leader with 83 goals. Carlsson’s milestone came amid a difficult night for Anaheim, which surrendered a three-goal advantage before Filip Hronek scored the game-winning goal on a two-man power play with 11 seconds remaining in overtime. The Ducks took control in the second period after AJ Greer opened the scoring at 15:52 of the first. Vancouver equalized at 6:36 of the second when Liam Ohgren benefited from a deflection off Anaheim defenseman Tristan Luneau. However, Jeff Malott restored the home side’s advantage 30 seconds later by redirecting a pass from Jackson LaCombe. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Ducks extended their lead to 3-1 through Beckett Sennecke’s power-play deflection at 15:44. Carlsson then capitalized on a rebound at 18:24, pushing the puck over the goal line after it bounced off Canucks defenseman Zeev Buium’s skate. The goal gave Anaheim a 4-1 advantage, but Vancouver gradually mounted the comeback. Brock Boeser reduced the deficit to two goals in the third period before Greer scored his second of the night to make it 5-2 at 12:23. Jamie Oleksiak responded 30 seconds later, bringing the Canucks within two. Jonathan Lekkerimaki subsequently scored twice in a 49-second stretch with the Ducks goaltender pulled, leveling the contest at 5-5 with 1:57 left in regulation. Vancouver outshot Anaheim 8-2 over the final 12 minutes of regulation and generated all four shots recorded during overtime. After penalties against Sennecke and Alex Killorn gave the visitors a five-on-three advantage, Hronek completed the comeback with the winning goal. Despite the defeat, Carlsson continued his productive start to the season. He has 15 points, including four goals and 11 assists, across 12 games, along with six six multipoint performances. The Ducks have now lost six of their last seven contests, dropping to a 5-6-1 record. Greer finished with two goals, LaCombe supplied three assists, and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves. Anaheim will look to recover during the ongoing homestand, with the Buffalo Sabres scheduled to visit Thursday before the Ducks host the Ottawa Senators on Sunday.

item.title: Scottish teams win opening tree European ties
item.description: [Getty Images] Scotland women have two wins out of two at the European Curling Championships in Ostrava in the Czech Republic after defeating Turkey 7-4. Fay Henderson's rink were two up after the first end but trailed by the the end of the third before picking up a three. Turkey got back within one after the sixth but a two at the next end got the Scots over the line. Henderson's team had opened with a comprehensive 12-3 victory over Denmark on Tuesday. They edged the opening two ends by single points before the Danes halved the deficit. However, the Scots took control of their opening, surging into a five-point lead by the close of the fourth end. Although Denmark scored two points in the fifth, Scotland ended the contest emphatically with a six-point haul in the sixth and final end. Scotland women face Sweden on Thursday (08:30 GMT), with the round-robin match live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app. Earlier on Wednesday, Scotland men triumphed 8-4 against the Netherlands in their opening tie. Grant Hardie's rink picked up two at the opening end and three at the third to lead 5-1. The Dutch were 6-4 down after six ends but Scotland picked up two more at the seventh to see out the win. Scotland men meet Belgium later on Wednesday. [BBC] New-look Scottish rinks eye European curling medals - watch live on BBC

item.title: ‘I only wanted one thing: to leave’ – AC Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos reflects on the end of his time at PSG
item.description: ‘I only wanted one thing: to leave’ – AC Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos reflects on the end of his time at PSG Despite spending three years at Paris Saint-Germain and scoring some crucial goals, Gonçalo Ramos (25) never quite established himself as an undisputed first-team regular during his time with Les Rouge et Bleu . A difficult situation to accept for the Portuguese striker, who, by joining AC Milan last summer, was ultimately able to turn a new page in his young career. And whilst leaving PSG – a “very close-knit” squad – was painful for him, the striker absolutely has no regrets about his decision. “I wanted to leave PSG, but in January it’s always more complicated to leave,” explained Ramos – whose desire to leave dated back to the 2026 winter transfer window – in an interview with Canal 11 . “It wasn’t the best option, even though I wanted it. Now I understand better. I was already at a stage where I wanted only one thing: to leave.” While the club refused to let him depart in the middle of the season, due to a lack of a replacement, Luis Campos had nevertheless “given his word” to the forward that “he would let me leave this summer” . A promise honoured a few months later by PSG’s sporting director. “During the World Cup, I was in touch with Jorge (Mendes, his agent) and Milan’s interest became apparent,” Ramos explained. “Manager Ruben Amorim came here and rang me. That was also very important. One day, Jorge Mendes rang me in the morning and said: ‘The deal is done.’” GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Tigers' Kevin McGonigle voted top AL rookie by his peers
item.description: DETROIT — The big one won’t be announced for a couple of weeks, but Kevin McGonigle keeps collecting all the rookie of the year run-up awards. The latest came Wednesday, Oct. 28, when he won, in a vote of his peers, the Players’ Choice Award for American League Outstanding Rookie. The Tigers’ 22-year-old shortstop/third baseman has also been named AL rookie of the year by Baseball America and the Sporting News. The Baseball Writers Association of America will present its rookie of the year award on Nov. 9. And as he did with the Players’ Choice vote, he is expected to beat out Cleveland’s Parker Messick and Chicago’s Munetaka Murakami for the AL rookie award. McGonigle produced one of the best rookie seasons in Tigers’ history in 2026, slashing .278/.376/.430. He led all American League players with a 7.1 bWAR. He reached base a club record 266 times in 156 games and filled up the stat sheet like no rookie since Ted Williams in 1939 with 168 hits, 28 doubles, 18 homers, 97 runs, 72 RBI, 95 walks and just 100 strikeouts. He joins Justin Verlander (2006), Austin Jackson (2010) and Michael Fulmer (2016) as Tigers’ winners of the Players’ Choice rookie award and will be the first since Fulmer to win BBWAA rookie of the year. item.title: Struggling Scunthorpe sack boss Butler
item.description: Andy Butler won 62 of his 127 matches as Scunthorpe manager [Getty Images] Scunthorpe United have sacked boss Andy Butler after a run of six defeats in seven National League games. The Iron were beaten 4-1 at Tamworth on Tuesday evening and are five points adrift of safety. The former Scunthorpe defender led the side to promotion from National League North in 2024-25 and then guided the team to a fifth-placed finish last season. However, they have not been able to replicate that sort of success this campaign and have already lost as many league matches as in the whole of last season. After their 10th defeat of the season at Tamworth, 42-year-old Butler questioned the application of the players. "I've protected them a lot. I think a little bit of harsh reality in terms of the players didn't look bothered, not all of them but a few of them," he told BBC Radio Humberside. "You're always going to be fighting an uphill battle if you haven't got players on the pitch who are giving 100%." In a statement on the club website Scunthorpe said Butler, who had three spells with the club as a player, "departs with our gratitude for his fantastic commitment, work rate and dedication". Scunthorpe face a trip to Lincolnshire rivals Boston United on Saturday.

item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Brewers’ Pat Murphy sends classy message to Rays despite painful Game 4 loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It was a tough Game 4 loss for the Milwaukee Brewers against the Tampa Bay Rays , but credit where credit is due. The Brewers manager Pat Murphy gave credit to the Rays for fighting back after their 4-3, 12-inning victory in the World Series on Tuesday. Despite the painful defeat, Murphy acknowledged Tampa Bay’s resilience and reminded his own team to prepare for another opportunity to clinch the championship. “We’re facing a club that has faced a lot of adversity this series, but give them credit, they bounced back well tonight,” Murphy said after the game. The Brewers still hold a 3-1 series lead and need one more victory to secure the first World Series title in franchise history. Milwaukee was set to finish the job when rookie Cooper Pratt hit a home run in the top of the 12th to give the Brewers a 3-2 lead. However, a fielding error by third baseman Joey Ortiz opened the door for Tampa Bay. Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson followed with singles that brought home two runs and ended the game. Reliever Shane Drohan struggled to close out the contest, allowing hits to all four batters he faced after Milwaukee had used several other bullpen arms. Additionally, Murphy refused to dwell on the setback, emphasizing that adversity comes with the challenge of winning a championship. “When you’re achieving something like this, it’s going to have its adversity,” Murphy said. “We had some things go our way yesterday; they had some things go their way today. item.title: Odegaard urges Arsenal to move on after Fleetwood upset
item.description: Fleetwood fans invade the pitch as they celebrate their team's penalty shootout win over Arsenal in the fourth round of the English League Cup (Darren Staples) Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard has insisted "we can't feel sorry for ourselves" and must move on quickly following their stunning loss away to fourth-tier Fleetwood in the League Cup. The Premier League champions crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible upset after the fourth-round tie finished 1-1 in normal time at Fleetwood's home ground of Highbury. Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out before teenage defender Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood's winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi's first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta made nine changes to his starting side but after a ragged first-half display he sent Norway midfielder Odegaard on for the second period. The visitors, last season's losing finalists, managed an improved performance but still missed several chances before teenage rising star Max Dowman was sent off five minutes from the end of normal time. "It's very frustrating to go out," Odegaard said after Fleetwood made a mockery of the 84 places between the clubs in the English football pyramid. "Obviously, the way we've played was not on the level. We need to do much, much better than we did. "Frustrating, but congratulations to Fleetwood and we look forward to the next game already and bounce back. "They did well so we have to give them credit, but... we need to do better. I thought we improved during the game, but again, we need to step up even more -- so that's a shame." Arsenal now just have days to get the defeat out of their system ahead of what promises to be a tough match at Liverpool on Sunday, with the Gunners having drawn level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City last weekend. "We can't feel sorry for ourselves. We need to move on -- we have a big game at the weekend, so bouncing back at the weekend is all we can do now," Odegaard added. Meanwhile, British media reports Wednesday said Arsenal would lodge an appeal against Dowman's red card with the Football Association and were hopeful of a decision being handed down prior to the trip to Anfield. The 16-year-old was dismissed for kicking out at Harrison Neal following a heavy challenge by the Fleetwood midfielder, with an unimpressed Arteta giving Dowman a strong word as he trudged off. "Something that we discussed already before the match," Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. jdg/nf

item.title: Fleetwood Town boss shares what Arteta said to him after cup defeat
item.description: Fleetwood Town boss shares what Arteta said to him after cup defeat Fleetwood Town manager Matt Lawlor has praised Mikel Arteta for his response to Arsenal’s League Cup defeat on Tuesday night. Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images Arsenal suffered a very disappointing defeat to League Two side Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night, exiting the League Cup in the fourth round. The loss was Arsenal’s second in two games against lower-league opposition, having also exited the FA Cup to Southampton earlier in 2026. Mikel Arteta was very clearly unhappy about his team’s elimination, but Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor suggested the Arsenal boss had been gracious to him in defeat. Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images “He shook my hand two or three times, and he was really, really gracious,” Lawlor said . “I can imagine it’s a really disappointing night for him, but the way that he acted with class is amazing there. “I would love to catch up with him, pick his brain, and learn off the best. But he’s been really busy with media and all the emotion, like the crowd, so we’ve not managed to cross paths. “But he said ‘well done’ in the tunnel briefly, and how well we did, and that was it. Obviously a show of class from him.” Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images Arteta may have had cause to be upset with the red card shown to Max Dowman , which Arsenal are appealing. But the decision came late in the game, and it likely didn’t affect the result. The Arsenal boss can only really be frustrated with himself and with his team’s failure to put away their many chances, so there would be no good reason to take that out on the opposition manager. This was just Fleetwood’s night, and the classy move was definitely to let them enjoy it. Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images

item.title: Journalist thinks the current Juventus formation has made them stronger
item.description: Journalist thinks the current Juventus formation has made them stronger Since switching to a 3-5-2 formation following the shock loss to Lazio , Juventus has found a degree of stability, particularly at the back. Luciano Spalletti has been constantly required to find solutions because his Juventus side has lacked balance and stability over recent seasons, and the manager now believes he has identified the right formation. The 3-5-2 makes Juventus difficult to break down, while also allowing the team to field both strikers at the same time. This is intended to help them create more chances and score more frequently. That attacking improvement has not fully materialised yet, but defensively, the Old Lady has become one of the hardest teams to score against, and they will be eager to maintain that record. Defensive Progress Under Spalletti So far, Juventus has performed well with the new system, although further tests lie ahead. Those upcoming matches will determine whether the 3-5-2 is genuinely the right approach or whether another tactical adjustment will eventually be required. For now, the team appears settled in the new structure. Journalist Gianni Balzarini has been impressed by what he has seen while Juventus plays in this formation, and he appears to support the idea of continuing with it. As quoted by Tuttojuve , he said: “Spalletti would like to continue with the 3-5-2, I actually said it in part, that is, it gives them more solidity. It’s basically the concept of the first one not conceding and then having the possibility of fielding two attackers at the same time or at least two players with an attacking inclination.” (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) A System Still Being Tested Balzarini’s assessment highlights the central appeal of the formation: it prioritises defensive solidity while retaining the flexibility to deploy two attacking players. For Juventus, that balance could prove valuable as the season progresses. However, the system must continue to deliver results against stronger opposition. If Juventus can combine their improved defensive organisation with greater cutting edge in attack, the 3-5-2 may become the foundation Spalletti has been searching for. Until then, the formation remains a promising but still unproven solution.

item.title: Yankees legend says he’s not welcome anymore: ‘I don’t know what happened’
item.description: Yankees legend Jorge Posada says he no longer feels “welcome” around his old team. Posada, a five-time All-Star and four-time World Series champion with the Yankees, was asked by Joel Sherman of the New York Post if he thought he could improve the Yankees’ “unacceptable” behavior by being around the team more. “I could, but I don’t think they want me there,” Posada said on “The Show” podcast. “I don’t feel welcome when I go there. Even in spring training...I don’t feel welcome. I don’t feel like they want me there so I don’t go.” Asked where he thought that “flowed” from, Posada added: “I don’t know. I don’t know what happened. I’d rather just move forward. My last season of my career was a really tough one when it comes to handling everything on my part and also the Yankees towards Jorge Posada so it’s tough to go back and feel that again.” Posada spent all 17 seasons of his career with the Yankees and was considered part of the “Core 4″ with Derek Jeter, Andy Pettitte and Mariano Rivera. Posada did attend the Yankees’ 78th Old-Timers’ Day on Aug. 8. He participated in the alumni game and hit a double. His comments come after several Yankees from that era, including Alex Rodriguez, CC Sabathia and former manager Joe Girardi, criticized the Yankees’ culture and level of accountability after they were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. item.title: Caitlin Clark surprises Indiana high school team with new Caitlin 1s
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Caitlin Clark gave local Indiana hoopers the surprise of a lifetime. Caitlin Clark didn’t just show up in Indiana, she completely took the place by storm. She’s built a fiercely loyal cult following that turns every single Fever game, whether it’s home or away, packing arenas with kids rocking her #22 jersey. But the wildest part about the whole Clark phenomenon is how little she lets the hype change her. You constantly see her sticking around long after the final buzzer just to autograph battered signs, high-five kids in the front row, and lean into local charity work. In an era where superstars can feel totally untouchable, she just feels like a kid who loves basketball. Caitlin Clark gifts Caitlin 1s to Indiana high school team The Zionsville girls got the shock of a lifetime when boxes of Caitlin 1s showed up in their locker room. The team posted a video to X showing the exact second they opened them, screaming, jumping around, hugging each other, and clutching their blue pairs. Their post said it all: “Really cool night for Zionsville Girls’ Basketball. Thank YOU, Nike and Caitlin Clark !” Getting your hands on a pair of Caitlin 1s had been next to impossible for some people. The Caitlin 1s vanished off the SNKRS app and store shelves in no time flat on drop day, with resale prices immediately shooting through the roof. And there’s already a queue of new colorways for the season, including the Iowa colours, which is a personal favourite of Clark’s and the Chiefs colourway that Travis Kelce loves . item.title: Passion and Legacy: Meet the owner of the largest Ohio State women’s sports memorabilia collection
item.description: Ohio State guard Jacy Sheldon standing next to Rachel Mansfield | Rachel Mansfield The world of sports is about anxiety. In basketball’s case, the clock winds down, time is limited to do something, anything, to get your team ahead while five people are dead set on stopping that very thing from happening. Then add in thousands of people watching, cheering or jeering and the best athletes prove themselves as ones who can silence the noise. When the moment requires it, stars step up and overcome that anxiety. They turn it into victory. It is Dec. 28, 2025 in Columbus, Ohio. Ohio State women’s basketball and the soon-to-be crowned National Champions the UCLA Bruins have a scheduled Big Ten matchup at the Schottenstein Center. The hallways of the arena are not yet overrun with people. Only security guards, red coats and concession stand workers hustle to make it to their stations. Before any buzzer sounds, whistle is blown or basketball is dribbled, there is a different kind of anxiety. It is not on the hardwood court but it stands a few feet outside of those empty, echoing, hallways. Some fans line up early to skip the food lines, catch a few moments of shootaround or on this afternoon just escape the cold. There is a basketball fan in the with a different motivation. Rachel Mansfield wants to get the autograph Bruins point guard Kiki Rice. That night, getting down to the court before Rice players left for the pregame locker room talk was on Mansfield’s No. 1 goal. “I got through the door, got down to [section ]124 as like Kiki [Rice] was getting ready to walk off,” Mansfield told Land-Grant Holy Land. “It’s like a rush.” Its a three-hour trip, one way, for Mansfield from her home in Northeast Ohio down to Columbus. That alone is an admirable trek to come see a favorite player alongside her team full of now WNBA players, but the journey is nothing new. That’s because Mansfield is also an Ohio State women’s basketball season ticket holder and collector of arguably the largest collection of Buckeye women’s sports cards and memorabilia. Everywhere you turn in Mansfield’s room, there is scarlet and gray. From signed cards by current Buckeyes like point guard Jaloni Cambridge and center Elsa Lemmilä to a framed, unbroken, sheet of cards from the 1993 National Championship runners-up team signed by the entire roster. That includes Basketball Hall of Fame guard Katie Smith. From a signed and inscribed replica of Buckeye legend Tracey Hall’s retirement banner, an item from the now closed Buckeye Cafe to a pair of game worn shorts from Amber Stoke when the Buckeyes played the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on the deck of the USS Yorktown naval ship on Nov. 9, 2012. Think of any era of Ohio State women’s basketball and Mansfield probably has something from it, if not multiple things. So, why the UCLA Bruins? Sure, the native Ohioan Mansfield loves Ohio State. item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Rays’ Nick Martinez drops mic with ‘dangerous’ claim after World Series Game 4 win appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Tampa Bay Rays stayed alive in the World Series after pulling off a come-from-behind win against the Milwaukee Brewers , 4-3, in Game 4 at Tropicana Field on Tuesday. The Rays needed 12 innings to prevent a sweep, with Ben Williamson delivering the game-winning hit with the bases loaded. His walk-off single drove in Nick Fortes. After the game, Williamson touted their resiliency and togetherness , stressing that they dug deep and kept fighting. History is not on the Rays’ side, as no team has clawed back from a 3-0 deficit in the World Series. Martinez, who started in Game 1, came out of the bullpen to relieve Tyler Wells. In 33 pitches in two innings, Martinez gave up one hit and had one strikeout. Manager Kevin Cash tipped his hat to the one-time All-Star. “I can’t say enough about Nick Martinez and the contributions he’s made all season long. item.title: What first six Commanders games have told us about rookie Sonny Styles
item.description: The Commanders used a top 10 NFL draft pick on a non-premium position. Selections that high are normally reserved for a handful of spots, valued above all others, including quarterback, edge rusher, cornerback, offensive tackle and, at times, receiver. An off-the-ball linebacker isn’t in the mix. Yet the Commanders confidently and without hesitation took Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles at No. 7 overall . There are exceptions to every rule. Styles was one. The athletic freak with an off-the-charts RAS was taken without hesitation, as a defensive anchor point for years to come. After giving up 35 unanswered points to the Bengals in the second-half of Sunday’s game, questions are starting to rain down on the Ravens. Unfortunately, Baltimore’s second-half meltdowns have now transcended multiple coaching staffs. Coming into Week 7, the team had already blown double-digit leads to the Saints and Browns. However, Sunday’s collapse was on a completely different level. The Ravens didn’t just get beat in the second half; they were completely annihilated. Fans and media are predictably rushing to play the blame game and rebuild the roster, but it’s too early in the season to be calling for sweeping changes, especially after three straight games with a backup quarterback. A 1-2 record without Lamar Jackson is closer to an expected result than an outright disaster. It’s less that the Ravens lost those games and more how they fell apart when their best was needed. With a locker room, coaching staff, and front office searching for answers, let’s look at what aspects of the 2026 Ravens should be of concern, but more importantly, where there could be some light at the end of this currently dark tunnel. item.title: LSU vs. Auburn: Week 8 Game MVP
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Jackson Harris #4 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) The LSU Tigers dominated on Saturday, and several players had a day. There are a couple who deserve to be highlighted. Let’s start with DJ Pickett. After the departure of Mansoor Delane, who was drafted in the top 10 of the NFL Draft, the expectation was for Pickett to become the next lockdown cornerback for the Tigers, and he has done just that. Against Auburn, Pickett allowed just one completion on five targets for a total gain of one yard. That’s a completion percentage of 20%. Pickett is a vital reason why the defense is having the success it is having. When you can put a player on one half of the field and just let him handle it, it frees up the other 10 players to be as deceptive as they need to be to cause chaos and confusion for opposing quarterbacks. The other player who has already received SEC recognition but needs to be highlighted some more is Sam Leavitt. Leavitt struggled to start the season, but over the last five weeks, he has been on a tear. He has completed over 70% of his passes in each game since the Texas A&M game. Because of this recent surge, he is now completing over 70% of his passes for the season, which would be the highest completion percentage of his career. Leavitt is also turning the corner when it comes to giving the ball away. For the second week in a row, he finished the game without having a turnover show up on the stat sheet. QB1 for the Tigers is showcasing the skills to make the argument that he is one of the best quarterbacks in the SEC. The game MVP is Jackson Harris. Harris is the WR1 for the Tigers, and his recent ascension has elevated the play of the entire offense. Without Harris emerging as a reliable pass-catching target for Leavitt, this offense would still be sputtering. Since the A&M game, Harris has 31 receptions, 517 yards, and seven touchdowns. Against Auburn, he finished the game with nine catches, 178 yards, and two touchdowns. He was a toenail shy of having a third touchdown and pushing that yardage total closer to 200 yards. Harris is rounding into form, and the deep-threat transfer from Hawaii is showing that his breakaway speed is translating to the SEC. So far this season, Harris is averaging 17.6 yards per catch. Elite. Who is your game MVP? If you were Lane Kiffin, how would you approach the bye week to get ready for Alabama? Share your thoughts in the comments.

(Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two massive wins in the NFC South, including one of the most unlikely blowouts in a while. Here is how each team did in Week 7 Tampa Bay Buccaneers : Against all odds, the Buccaneers beat the Panthers 43-13 in Charlotte. Not sure anyone expected this result, but it is the NFC South, so maybe that’s on me. This game marked the return of Baker Mayfield to the lineup, but hilariously, he only threw 11 times, completing 7 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. And yes, he did play most of the game. Bucky Irving was the star for the Buccaneers offense, getting over 100 yards rushing and two touchdowns. I’ll talk a bit more about the Buccaneers defense in the next section. Carolina Panthers : And then we have the Panthers. This was Carolina’s worst game this season, and with the defense struggling, the offensive issues only made it worse. Bryce Young was sacked 5 times, threw two interceptions, the run game was horrible, and the Panthers fumbled once. This was one of those games Carolina should put behind them, but their first-place lead just got much smaller. Atlanta Falcons : With the upset of the week, the Falcons somehow beat the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. What made this win even more impressive for the Falcons was that they didn’t need to rely on Bijan Robinson’s rushing ability to win, which has been their recipe for success. Michael Penix had a strong game, controlling the offense and avoiding turnovers, while the defense forced turnovers that made the difference. New Orleans Saints : Due to the Buccaneers’ win, the Saints are now last in the division after their loss to the Steelers. This wasn’t as embarrassing as some of their previous losses, but it made clear once again that the season’s issues persist. What made it worse was that the Saints’ massive red-zone improvement regressed. Heading into the bye, the team must make changes across the roster, and although Kellen Moore may be safe, one more loss could end his time in New Orleans.

item.description: Rich Rebels Aiden Weston (10) celebrates with Rich Rebels Wilkes Weston (4) after scoring a touchdown during a 1A high school football 8-player state championship game against the Milford Tigers at Zions Bank Stadium in Herriman on Saturday, Nov. 15, 2025. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News 1A Quarterfinals No. 9 Parowan (2-9) at No. 1 Duchesne (9-1) 1A quarterfinals Friday, Oct. 30, 5 p.m. Parry’s Power Guide: Duchesne by 58 All-time series: Duchesne leads 16-4 since 1989 Last meeting: Duchesne won 40-20 at Duchesne (Sept. 30, 2022) What Parowan needs to do to win Parowan comes in playing its best football. The Rams lost 39-35 at North Sevier on Oct. 15, then went back to the same field eight days later and won 47-6 in the first round. That was their highest-scoring game of the season and their first win since Sept. 11. Parowan’s record looks worse than its season has been. Four of its nine losses came by a combined 15 points: 35-28 at Lincoln County (Nev.), 30-27 to 2A ALA, 15-14 at 1A Milford and 39-35 at North Sevier. The Rams also beat No. 7 seed Gunnison Valley 15-7. Against the rest of the 1A quarterfinal field, though, they were shut out four times: 45-0 at North Summit, 49-0 at Kanab, 49-0 at Beaver and 48-0 to Enterprise. Duchesne beat all four of those teams. To pull the upset, Parowan has to shorten the game and protect the ball. Tyrel Vest (517 yards, 8 TDs) needs enough carries for long drives that keep Duchesne’s offense on the sideline. Turnovers are the biggest risk. Parowan’s quarterbacks have thrown 14 interceptions, and Tyson Bettridge completes 39% of his passes. Duchesne’s defense has 19 interceptions and seven defensive touchdowns, so every mistake could turn into points. When Bettridge does connect, it’s usually a big play: he averages 16.2 yards per completion. Gradey Osborne (17.9 yards per catch) and Benson Haynie (5 TDs) are his best targets. On defense, Hagen Evans (69 tackles) and Cooper Heath (65) have to tackle well against a Duchesne running game that averages 7.5 yards per carry. What Duchesne needs to do to win Duchesne just needs to play the way it has all season. The Eagles lead 1A in scoring offense (43.6 ppg) and scoring defense (8.4 ppg), and they won the 1A North outright at 4-0. Their only loss was 18-13 at South Summit, a 2A quarterfinalist, in the season opener. They’ve won nine straight since. Duchesne went 6-0 against the other 1A quarterfinalists and outscored them 226-59. That includes a 24-15 win at Beaver, the team that knocked Duchesne out in last year’s semifinals, and a 28-0 win over No. 2 seed Kanab. The Eagles have held eight of 10 opponents to 15 points or fewer and have three shutouts. Outside 1A, they beat 4A Cottonwood 69-0 and Ignacio, Colo., 73-0. The running game leads the offense. Duchesne has run the ball 333 times and passed 112 times, and it has 45 rushing touchdowns. Kyson Despain has 1,391 yards and 20 touchdowns at 7.3 yards per carry.
